tagline: The FL Players league newsletter · est. 2008
headline: One Free Agent Would Have Flipped Four Games, James Wins on Sunday Night, and Colt Scores 130.16
dek: Inside: Brett over John on the kickers, the wire flips, what the night games decided and hold this week, the division races, the what-if tracker, the bracket if the season ended today, position groups and who is on IR.
lead:
Ted Hurst III scored 20.1 for Tampa Bay while unrostered in this league, and he would have turned four of the week's six losses into wins: T.J.'s, Austin's, Nase's and John's.

James beat Nase 96.86 to 90.36 to get to 9-2, and the game turned on Sunday night (see primetime). Anthony won the rematch of last year's final, 84.00 to 72.10, for his fourth straight win. Colt scored 130.16, the high score of the week, with nothing left on his bench.

The closest game went to Brett, 120.64 to 115.80 over John, and the kickers decided it.

managers.text: Beat Nase 96.86 to 90.36, a score under the week's median, behind Javonte Williams (22.6), George Kittle (16.9) and Tyler Bass (14.0). Seth McGowan started for 1.3 and left Thursday's game with a hamstring injury; as of Wednesday he did not practice and is questionable. His previous 9-2 starts: the 2017 title and playoff trips in 2020 and 2022.
managers.next: Week 12: Mikey. James has won four straight in the series, leads it 11-4, and is a 54% favorite.
managers.outlook: 97% to win Division 2 and take a bye, and 30% for the title.

managers.text: Beat Austin (see the lead). Chuba Hubbard (26.0), Malik Nabers (15.0) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (12.2) led it, and J.J. McCarthy had 14.22 on the bench. He leads the league in points, 1,292.7. Kenneth Walker III is out again for Thursday's game with a groin injury.
managers.next: Week 12: John. Anthony leads the series 8-6 and is a 68% favorite.
managers.outlook: 99% to win Division 1 and the best title odds in the league, 33%.

managers.text: Beat T.J. 97.02 to 77.76 behind Emmett Johnson (22.3), Cam Ward (22.22) and Christian McCaffrey (13.2). Antonio Williams had 16.7 on the bench and Luther Burden started for 2.3. He then dropped Ward for Chimere Dike (see the moves). He has 36.12 in already for week 12 from Wednesday's game.
managers.next: Week 12: Colt, the game of the week. Colt has won the last two meetings and leads the series 10-9; Buckley is a 61% favorite.
managers.outlook: 95% for the playoffs and 3% to catch James for Division 2.

managers.text: Beat Joey 130.16 to 92.84 (see the lead). Travis Kelce (22.4), C.J. Stroud (20.46) and Ladd McConkey (18.2) led it. He added Brandon Aiyuk this week. Puka Nacua is in his IR slot after MCL surgery that may end his season, and one host on a popular show Monday (Nov 23) said he doesn't think Nacua plays another down for the Rams. As of Wednesday Derrick Henry, in his lineup, was limited in the concussion protocol, and Jordan Addison did not practice with his thumb injury; both are questionable.
managers.outlook: 61% for the playoffs, holding the 4 seed today.

managers.text: Beat John 120.64 to 115.80, the closest game of the week, with nothing left on his bench. Jonah Coleman (32.9), Parker Washington (14.3) and the Denver defense (13.0) led it. With J.K. Dobbins suspended, Coleman has Denver's backfield to himself; on a popular show Monday (Nov 23) he was the betting favorite for Offensive Rookie of the Year. Without kickers John wins this one, the what-if rule; Wil Lutz outscored John's kicker 8 to 3 (see the what-if tracker). His previous 6-5 starts: a 2020 playoff trip and the 2024 title.
managers.next: Week 12: Austin. Brett has won the last three meetings and Austin leads the series 13-12. Brett is at 45%.
managers.outlook: 69% for the playoffs, the 5 seed today.

managers.text: Lost 130.16 to 92.84 to Colt. Breece Hall (17.5), Jameson Williams (17.3) and the Houston defense (15.0) led it. Geno Smith had 19.44 on the bench and Rachaad White started for 0.0. That is four straight losses after a 6-1 start, and he holds the 6 seed by a game.
managers.next: Week 12: T.J. Joey has won eight straight in the series, leads it 13-4, and is a 51% favorite.
managers.outlook: 63% for the playoffs, and under 1% to catch Anthony in Division 1.

managers.text: Beat Mikey 130.06 to 108.90 behind Gibbs (25.8), Patrick Mahomes (24.96) and George Pickens (20.3). Two straight wins. The San Francisco defense he claimed for $3 scored 15.0 on Sunday night.
managers.next: Week 12: Nase. Scott leads the series 11-7 and is a 70% favorite.

managers.text: Lost 84.00 to 72.10 to Anthony. Joe Burrow scored 19.9 on Monday night, 12.87 under his average, and Ja'Marr Chase 5.6, 12.38 under his. Bucky Irving (17.5) and Brandon Aubrey (9.0) were next, and Jordyn Tyson started for 1.5. He claimed the Giants defense for $6 and added Dallas Goedert. There was debate on Monday (Nov 23) over whether New Orleans had soft-benched him.
managers.next: Week 12: Brett. Austin is a 55% favorite.

managers.text: Lost 120.64 to 115.80 to Brett (see Brett). Ashton Jeanty (25.4), Purdy (22.2) and Evans (19.9) led it. Jeanty got a vote as a possible fantasy playoff hero on a popular show Monday (Nov 23); the Tampa Bay defense scored 0.0 and Bo Nix had 11.5 on the bench. As of Wednesday Purdy did not practice with an ankle injury and Evans did not practice with his Achilles, and both are questionable.

Lost 97.02 to 77.76 to Buckley. CeeDee Lamb (24.7), Daniels (17.06) and Croskey-Merritt (14.7) led it, Jared Goff had 20.36 on the bench, and J.K. Dobbins started for 0.0. Denver then suspended Dobbins for a game, and T.J. claimed Justice Hill for him (see the moves). As of Wednesday Bowers was limited with an ankle injury and is questionable, with his coach optimistic about Sunday night, and Diggs missed practice for personal reasons and is questionable.
managers.outlook: 3% for the playoffs and 11% to finish last.

managers.text: Lost 96.86 to 90.36 to James (see primetime), with nothing better on his bench. DJ Moore (19.1), Bryce Young (15.96) and Chris Olave (14.7) led it. Jonathan Taylor scored 4.7 on Thursday night, 10.49 under his average, and the Chargers defense 1.0.
managers.outlook: 1% for the playoffs and 15% to finish last.

managers.text: Lost 130.06 to 108.90 to Scott. Dak Prescott (35.9), Saquon Barkley (13.5) and Nico Collins (13.3) led it, and the Minnesota defense scored 0.0.

tags.t: Most points left on the bench

moves.intro: No trades, with the deadline at week 13. T.J. replaced a suspended back, Colt picked up a receiver on the move, and Buckley let a quarterback go.

items.title: Justice Hill for $5
items.text: T.J. claimed Justice Hill for $5 and dropped J.K. Dobbins, who started for 0.0 in week 11 and is suspended for week 12. On a popular waiver show Tuesday (Nov 24), Hill was called surprisingly explosive at 29.
items.verdict: Buckley bid $0 on Hill and lost it.

items.title: Brandon Aiyuk
items.text: Colt added Brandon Aiyuk as a free agent, dropping Austin Ekeler. He also claimed Tyler Allgeier for $0, added the Jets defense and Jason Sanders, and dropped Tyler Shough.
items.verdict: Aiyuk's new team is Washington, per Wednesday's headline.

items.title: Cam Ward out
items.text: Buckley dropped Cam Ward, who scored 22.22 for him in week 11, for Chimere Dike, and added Konata Mumpfield and the Cleveland defense. The same Tuesday show (Nov 24) named Dike as the receiver it would rather add than Ted Hurst.

items.title: Giants defense, $6
items.text: Austin's $4 bid on the Jets defense failed, and his $6 bid on the Giants won, over Colt's $6.
items.verdict: The biggest bid of the week.

trends.title: What eleven weeks means here
trends.text: Every team that was 8-3 or better after eleven weeks has made the playoffs, 27 of 27. 7-4 teams made it 88% of the time, 6-5 teams 69%, 5-6 teams 33%, 4-7 teams once in 21 tries, and none of the 33 teams at 3-8 or worse.

trends.title: Scoring
trends.text: Week 11 averaged 101.4 a team, down from 109.7 in week 10.

trends.title: The wire
trends.text: Ted Hurst III, unrostered that week, would have flipped four losses: T.J.'s in place of DK Metcalf (0.7), Austin's in place of Jordyn Tyson (1.5), Nase's in place of Rome Odunze (6.5), and John's in place of Emeka Egbuka (2.8). Waiver timing is not checked. The popular advice on Monday and Tuesday (Nov 23 and 24) was that Hurst's week was worth a roster spot but not a start.

history.title: Week 11, all time
history.text: The highest week 11 score on record is Anthony's 156.08 against Nase in 2021. The biggest week 11 blowout was Buckley over Nase, 144.98 to 68.94, in 2018. The closest was Austin over Colt, 95 to 94, in 2012.

ahead: Game of the week: Buckley against Colt, 7-4 against 6-5 in Division 2, with Colt holding the 4 seed and both of them starting players on Thanksgiving. Also: Brett against Austin for a wild card, and T.J. against Joey, who has won eight straight in the series. The trade deadline is week 13.

features.label: Primetime
features.title: The night games, both ways
features.dek: Which matchups last week's primetime games touched and changed, and who has what riding on the holiday slate.

blocks.text: Week 11, looking back
Thursday night, Indianapolis at Houston, touched four of the six matchups. Sunday night, Minnesota against San Francisco, and Monday night, Cincinnati at Washington, touched all six.
Sunday night outscored the margin in one game. George Kittle scored 16.9 for James, who beat Nase by 6.50, and Nase had nobody playing in it.

The two biggest primetime hauls both came in losses. John got 42.1 on Sunday night from Brock Purdy and Mike Evans and lost by 4.84. T.J. got 38.26 on Monday night from Jayden Daniels, Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Stefon Diggs and lost by 19.26.
Week 12, looking ahead

items: Already played, Wednesday, Green Bay at the Rams: Buckley banked 36.12 from Jordan Love and Blake Corum. T.J. has 14.5 from Christian Watson, who left with a concussion.

Thanksgiving, Chicago at Detroit: five matchups. Scott starts Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta, 34.04 projected, against Nase's Rome Odunze at 10.75. Joey has Caleb Williams and Jameson Williams, 32.2, and T.J. has nobody in it. In the game of the week, Buckley's Luther Burden and Jake Bates, 21.89, go against Colt's D'Andre Swift, 13.48.
Thanksgiving, Philadelphia at Dallas: Mikey has Dak Prescott and Saquon Barkley, 35.3 projected, against James's Javonte Williams, 18.23.

Thanksgiving night, Kansas City at Buffalo: all six matchups. James starts Josh Allen and Tyler Bass, 27.23, and Mikey has nobody in it. Scott has Patrick Mahomes and Khalil Shakir, 22.23, and Buckley's Emmett Johnson, 17.38, goes against Colt's Travis Kelce, 7.85.
Black Friday, Denver at Pittsburgh: Brett starts Jonah Coleman, Wil Lutz and the Denver defense, 30.97 projected, against Austin's Jaylen Warren, 11.54.
Sunday night, Las Vegas at Cleveland: T.J.'s Brock Bowers, 12.08 projected if he plays, John's Ashton Jeanty and Buckley's Cleveland defense.

Monday night, Carolina at Tampa Bay: John's Tetairoa McMillan and Tampa Bay defense, 18.84, against Anthony's Chuba Hubbard and Chase McLaughlin, 23.0, so that matchup may still be open for the last game of the week. Austin has Bucky Irving at 19.09.

features.label: The races
features.title: Two divisions, two byes
features.dek: The byes go to the division winners, not the two best records.

blocks.text: Anthony is two games up on Joey with three weeks left, and Joey has lost four straight. Nobody else in the division is better than 4-7.
James is two games clear of Buckley. Behind them, Colt and Brett at 6-5 and Scott and Austin at 5-6 are playing for wild cards.
Chances come from [10,000 simulated finishes](/odds) of the season after week 11. A tie for a division is broken on points in the model.

features.label: The what-if tracker
features.title: The what-if tracker, week 11 update
features.dek: Two rule changes that keep coming up in the chat, tracked every week. Week 9 carried the full tables; this is what moved since.

blocks.text: One game flipped without kickers this week: Brett beat John by 4.84, and the kickers scored 8 to 3. It is the third game this season that kickers have decided against John, and without them he would be 7-4 and the 4 seed. The no-kicker field changed with it: John and Scott are in, Brett and Colt out. Last week it was John and T.J. in, Austin and Colt out. Mikey stretched his lead in kicker points to 110, and Anthony still has the fewest, now 73.

With a median game, Scott now has the most top-half weeks in the league, 8 of 11, and would be the 3 seed. Brett is back inside that field, so the only change from the real standings is Scott in and Colt out.
The full no-kicker and median tables ran in week 9 and stay on the site: the [standings page](/standings) has the median toggle and the [trackers page](/trackers) has the kicker file.

First round: 3 Buckley against 6 Joey, and 4 Colt against 5 Brett.
First team out: Scott, a game behind Joey at 5-6, with the second-most points in the league, 166.54 more than Joey.

features.label: Position groups
features.title: What each spot has actually produced
features.dek: Two different questions. From the lineup is what a manager has banked at that position over eleven weeks from whoever he started, with the flex counting toward whichever position filled it. On paper is every point the roster as it stands today has scored this season on a roster in this league, including points scored for a previous owner.

blocks.text: T.J. is first from receiver and last from running back, 101.6 behind eleventh. On paper his backs have scored 104, also last, so that one is the roster and not the lineup.

Austin is the widest gap again. He has the most from quarterback and the least from tight end, and his tight ends are the best room on paper at 195 with 39 of it started. Juwan Johnson has 68.7 of that and none of it came in Austin's lineup.
Buckley is the other split: the best running back room on paper at 607 and eleventh from receiver.

Through week 11, from Sleeper box scores, read Thursday morning. From the lineup counts only players actually started that week. On paper counts every point the current roster has scored this season while rostered in this league, whoever owned the player at the time.

blocks.text: Each team has one IR slot. Seven of the twelve are using it.
Anthony, T.J., Brett, Nase and Mikey have the slot open.
